approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that would let ASIC charge more for its regulatory work.
The package would raise the maximum fees ASIC can collect and create new fees for tasks under several Acts, including the Life Insurance Act 1995 and the Insurance Act 1973.
ASIC could set different fees based on the entity type and the complexity of the application, and charge extra for changing or cancelling an SMSF auditor's registration.
Raises the caps on fees ASIC can recover for regulatory services.
Expands the definition of chargeable matter to include new fees under the Life Insurance Act 1995, the Insurance Act 1973 and the SIS Act.
Allows regulations to prescribe different fees based on entity type.
Allows regulations to set fees according to low, medium or high complexity.
Lets ASIC determine by legislative instrument whether an application is low, medium or high complexity.
Permits ASIC to charge additional fees for varying, revoking or cancelling an approved SMSF auditor's registration.
Entities that pay fees to ASIC for regulatory services, including approved SMSF auditors.

This bill amends the Credit Fees Act to allow ASIC to charge different fees based on the type of entity, enabling full cost recovery for specific regulatory activities such as processing licence or registration applications. Complementary amendments are made in three related bills.
